content.comment_body: Can someone review this circuit and explain how I can achieve the desired outcome? Inputs 1 and 2 are pressure switches connected to two fans. I need to confirm they are open before the fans start. Currently, my setup does check if they are open but starts the fan after the switches are engaged. I want the fans to start because the pressure switches are intended to trigger other functions in the program. Hope that clarifies my request.

See if this example meets your needs. When the fans turn on, each associated pressure switch should be open. Fans start and a 3-second bridging period begins. If, after 3 seconds, the fans haven't built up pressure, they shut off. Likewise, if a pressure switch closes and then reopens, the fan is also turned off.
This setup works to some extent, but when one pressure switch is triggered, only one fan operates while the other turns off.
Are you looking for both pressure switches to control each fan? The program structure, especially with the two S/R blocks, confused me. Your description was a bit unclear as well.
Is this what you had in mind?
Apologies, I should have mentioned the fans share a common output. Sorry for the confusion—it's working perfectly now, thank you.
Just remove Q2 and everything should function correctly.

analysis.insight_summary: The discussion centers around configuring input logic for starting fans based on pressure switches in an automation setup. Initial confusion about the intended behavior resulted in misunderstandings, but the resolution underlined the importance of clear documentation, simple logic diagrams, and possibly more user-friendly programming resources or examples.
analysis.user_expectations: The user wants a circuit setup that confirms both pressure switches are open before fan activation and allows both fans to run from a shared output while staying true to the required control logic.
